frames.narration: Worker A starts a job that needs a lock. It has an open session, and it asks the leader to create an ephemeral, sequential key /lock/n-. Five servers are in the cluster, so a write needs 3.
The leader appends the write to its log and sends it to the followers. It commits as soon as 3 of the 5 servers, itself included, have stored it, without waiting for the slowest ones.
A's key is /lock/n-001, the lowest, so A holds the lock. The token is 7, the log position of its key. Worker B asks for a key as well and gets /lock/n-002 at position 8, so B must wait.
B does not poll. It sets a watch on the key just before its own, /lock/n-001, so it is woken only when that key changes. With 100 waiters, each one watches only its predecessor.
A uses the lock and writes to the protected storage, sending its token 7 with the write. The storage remembers the highest token it has seen and accepts 7.
Now worker A stalls, for example in a long pause. It stops sending heartbeats, and after the session timeout the session tracker declares the session dead.
The leader deletes A's ephemeral key by an ordinary write, committed by 3 of 5 like any other. That change triggers B's watch, and B is told once.
B reads the children of /lock, using a synchronised read so it cannot see an old list, and finds that n-002 is now the lowest. B holds the lock with token 8 and writes to the storage.

A wakes up still believing that it holds the lock and tries to write with token 7. The storage has seen 8 and refuses it. The lock service could not stop the paused process, but the fencing token did.
